page: Microsoft Azure E8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory allocations and fast local scratch storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The compute configuration provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 instruction cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache, alongside specialized instruction extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math acceleration, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

The instance delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. To support I/O-intensive temporary operations, the server is provisioned with 472 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without a dedicated hardware GPU accelerator, utilizing standard cloud networking without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic and operational benchmarks position the instance within the average tier across general compute metrics, reflecting its 8-vCPU footprint. The server logged a Geekbench single-core score of 1784.0, a multi-core score of 7007.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 14263.3. Memory throughput benchmarks show uncached read speeds of 67.01 GB/sec and uncached write speeds of 45.91 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput key-value operations such as Redis SET operations at 11.41 million operations per second. While smaller language models leverage CPU matrix extensions effectively, larger models experience significant throughput attenuation due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

Cost efficiency is aligned with enterprise memory density and included local NVMe performance. The integration of 472 GB of fast NVMe storage reduces external block storage requirements for cache tiers and staging disks. Microsoft Azure E8ds_v6 is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, relational database hosting, in-memory caching layers, static web serving, and ETL data staging.
